response.report:
EXAM: Chest radiograph, one view, 2026-11-20
CLINICAL INDICATION: Known lung nodule under surveillance. Admitted with fever. Portable film. Has the nodule changed?
ORDERING PROVIDER: Dr. S. Whitfield (synthetic), medical oncology
COMPARISON: Chest radiograph, 2026-08-21
TECHNIQUE: Current AP. Prior PA. Projection differs from the prior. Current film is underexposed. Both films are mildly rotated. Patient position (upright vs supine or semi-erect) is not shown on either image, and the current AP appears lordotic. Comparability is limited.

LOOK AT FIRST:
- None. No finding is flagged time-sensitive. Review priority order: F1 right lower zone opacity, F4 right hilum, F2 right hemidiaphragm contour.

FINDINGS (systematic read, done blind to the indication):
- Airway / lungs: Current: trachea is poorly seen through the underexposed upper mediastinum, with no gross displacement. Hazy, ill-defined opacity in the right lower zone with apparent right basal volume loss, reaching the lower right mid zone on the current film. It obscures the right heart border and medial right hemidiaphragm and is present on both studies (F1). Indeterminate. Both reads agree it cannot be called as changed or unchanged. Coarse linear and reticular markings in the left mid and lower zones on both studies (F6), seen on one of two blind reads. No new confluent opacity in the left lung. No pneumothorax. Small nodules and fine interstitial change cannot be excluded on the underexposed current film. Prior: similar hazy, partly linear right lower zone opacity with apparent right basal volume loss. Tracheal air column roughly midline to slightly right, within the range expected for mild rotation.
- Mediastinum / hila: Aortic knuckle is prominent with an unfolded aortic contour on both studies. The upper mediastinum looks wider on the AP current film. The two reads disagreed on this finding (F5), so it is indeterminate. The apparent widening is expected with AP projection and is not called as a change. Right hilar and infrahilar prominence is continuous with the right lower zone opacity on both studies (F4). Indeterminate. Only one of two reads identified it. Vessels, adjacent lung opacity and a hilar lesion cannot be separated, and size and change cannot be called. Left hilum is not clearly enlarged on the current film and is unremarkable on the prior.
- Pleura: Current: lateral right costophrenic sulcus is aerated and pointed, while the medial right base is opaque. Subpulmonic or layering pleural fluid is not excluded. Left costophrenic angle is sharp. Prior: aerated pocket at the lateral right base with opacity medial and inferior to it. Right pleural fluid or thickening is not excluded. Left costophrenic angle is sharp. No pneumothorax on either film. Right hemidiaphragm contour is high and indistinct medially on both studies, with an aerated lateral sulcus (F2). The two reads disagreed on this finding, so it is indeterminate. Interval change cannot be judged because apparent height differs with projection and beam angle. Left dome is sharp. No free gas is identified, but the upper abdomen is underexposed on the current film.
- Heart: Cardiac silhouette appears prominent on the PA prior and enlarged on the AP current (F3). Indeterminate. Both reads agree change is not comparable because AP projection magnifies the heart. Right heart border is obscured on both films. Cardiothoracic ratio on the prior is for radiologist measurement.
- Bones / soft tissue: No displaced rib fracture or gross destructive bone lesion on either film. Bone detail is limited on the current film by underexposure. Chest wall soft tissue is prominent on the current film. No soft tissue gas. No lines, tubes, pacemaker or other internal device identified. No new device since the prior.

INTERVAL CHANGE:
- Changed: None can be called. F1, F3, F4 and F5 are present on both studies, but size or density change is not comparable (PA vs underexposed AP). F2 is indeterminate, and the two reads disagreed on it.
- Unchanged: Coarse linear and reticular markings in the left mid and lower zones have a similar distribution on both studies (F6, seen on one of two reads). Density was not compared because of the exposure difference.

RECIST 1.1: Not computed on radiographs.

CAN'T DETERMINE:
- Has the right lower zone opacity changed in size or density since the prior? | Reason: Prior is PA and current is AP and underexposed. Projection and exposure differences can make a basal opacity look larger or denser. | Recommend: CT chest, or repeat PA and lateral when the patient is able. (Read A, F1)
- Is there a right pleural effusion, including a subpulmonic component, and has it changed? | Reason: The high, indistinct right basal contour with an aerated lateral sulcus could reflect subpulmonic fluid, an elevated hemidiaphragm, or basal volume loss. A frontal film alone cannot separate these, and patient position on the current AP is not shown. | Recommend: Lateral or right lateral decubitus view, ultrasound of the right base, or CT chest. (Read A)
- Is there a right hilar or infrahilar mass or adenopathy underlying the right basal opacity and volume loss? | Reason: The right hilum merges with the adjacent opacity on both films. Mild rotation and the AP projection make hilar size unreliable. | Recommend: CT chest, with contrast if appropriate. (Read A)
- Has heart size changed? | Reason: AP projection magnifies the heart, and cardiothoracic ratio is valid on PA films only. The right heart border is also obscured on both studies. | Recommend: Repeat PA film when the patient is able, or echocardiography if clinically relevant. (Read A, F3)
- Is the right hemidiaphragm truly elevated, or is the contour formed by subpulmonic fluid or a process below the diaphragm? | Reason: The true diaphragm is not separately visible on a frontal film. The lordotic AP beam angle on the current film also alters the apparent dome height. | Recommend: Ultrasound of the right upper quadrant and right base, or CT covering the chest and upper abdomen. (Read A, F2)
- Are there small nodules or fine interstitial changes in either lung on the current study? | Reason: The current film is underexposed with heavy soft tissue overlap, and the clavicles project over the apices. Small nodules cannot be confirmed or excluded. | Recommend: CT chest, or repeat PA and lateral with adequate exposure. (Read A)
- Has the heart enlarged since the prior? | Reason: Prior is PA and current is AP. AP projection magnifies the heart, and the right heart border is obscured on both films. | Recommend: Repeat PA and lateral when the patient is able, or CT chest. (Read B, F3)
- Has the right lower zone opacity grown, shrunk, or stayed the same? | Reason: Projection differs (PA then AP) and the current film is underpenetrated. Size and density change cannot be reported across these differences. | Recommend: Repeat PA and lateral with good inspiration, or CT chest. (Read B, F1)
- Is the high right hemidiaphragm contour a truly elevated diaphragm, a subpulmonic effusion, or lower lobe volume loss? | Reason: A frontal film alone cannot separate these. Patient position on the current AP film is unknown, and fluid layers out when supine. | Recommend: Lateral and right lateral decubitus views, ultrasound of the right base, or CT chest. (Read B)
- Is the upper mediastinum truly wider on the current study? | Reason: AP projection, possible mild rotation, and underexposure each widen or blur the mediastinal contour. | Recommend: Repeat PA film, or CT chest if there is clinical concern. (Read B, F5)
- Are there small lung nodules or a hilar abnormality on the current study? | Reason: The current film is underpenetrated and low in contrast, with overlying soft tissue shadows. Small nodules and hilar detail cannot be assessed, and the right hilum is partly obscured by adjacent opacity on both studies. | Recommend: Review the source image in PACS with windowing; CT chest if a nodule or hilar lesion needs to be excluded. (Read B)
- Is there a retrocardiac opacity? | Reason: Vertebrae are not visible behind the heart on the current film, and a frontal view alone cannot clear this area. | Recommend: Lateral view or CT chest. (Read B)

IMPRESSION:
1. Hazy, ill-defined right lower zone opacity with apparent right basal volume loss, present on both studies (F1). Indeterminate. Size and density change cannot be judged because the prior is PA and the current is an underexposed AP. A new process within it cannot be confirmed or excluded.
2. Right hilar and infrahilar prominence continuous with the right lower zone opacity on both studies (F4). Indeterminate. Hilar size and change cannot be called. Only one of two reads identified this finding.
3. High, indistinct right hemidiaphragm contour with an aerated lateral right sulcus on both studies (F2). Indeterminate. The two reads disagreed. Subpulmonic fluid, true elevation and basal volume loss cannot be separated on frontal films.
4. Surveillance question (has the nodule changed?): no discrete nodule can be identified and matched on both films, so change in the nodule cannot be judged. The prior report describes a nodular opacity (no side or zone given), which the images do not establish. The hazy right lower zone opacity has not been adopted as the nodule. Small nodules cannot be excluded on the underexposed current film.
5. The prior report lists a small pleural effusion (no side given). No definite meniscus or blunted lateral costophrenic angle is seen on either side on either film, and an effusion has not been adopted as a finding. A right subpulmonic component remains undetermined.
6. Cardiac silhouette appears enlarged on the AP current vs prominent on the PA prior (F3). Indeterminate. Change is not comparable because of projection.
7. Prominent aortic knuckle on both studies. The apparent upper mediastinal widening on the AP current is not called as a change (F5). Indeterminate. The two reads disagreed.
8. Coarse linear and reticular markings in the left mid and lower zones, similar in distribution on both studies (F6). Seen on one of two reads.

RECOMMENDATIONS:
- CT chest, with contrast if appropriate, to address the right lower zone opacity, right hilum, right pleura and hemidiaphragm, and small nodules. No interval is specified in the findings; attending to set the timing.
- Repeat PA and lateral chest radiograph with adequate exposure and good inspiration when the patient is able.
- Lateral or right lateral decubitus view, or ultrasound of the right base and right upper quadrant, for the subpulmonic fluid and hemidiaphragm questions. No interval is specified in the findings; attending to set the timing.
- Review the source images in PACS with windowing. Echocardiography if heart size is clinically relevant.

AI DRAFT: requires resident review and attending signature.
